key_insight: Large-scale circulation in turbulent convection has stable states with a relaxational mode and damped oscillatory modes that turbulence continually excites.
engineering_relevance: A reduced stochastic model offers a tractable way to interpret circulation oscillations and rare flow reversals in buoyancy-driven thermal systems.
method: Derive three coupled stochastic equations from the Boussinesq momentum and temperature equations.
Linearize around stable circulation states to identify intrinsic decay and oscillation modes.
Compare mode behavior and Rayleigh-number scalings with thin-disk convection experiments.
evidence_signal: Thin-disk experiments resolve both relaxational and oscillatory mode types and show their predicted Rayleigh-number scalings.
watch_item: Validation is reported for a thin-disk cell; applicability to other geometries and quantitative prediction of rare transitions require further testing.
paper_title: Stable eigenmodes of the Large-scale circulation in Turbulent Convection
